subject: Follow-up: Redwood Standard Demo — recap + eval next steps
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@northstar-ai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 6:12 PM
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood Standard Demo — recap + eval next steps

Alyssa — thanks again for the time today.

Quick recap of what we showed (and why it maps to what you described):
1) Low-latency streaming chat on the Hosted API
   - Emphasis: predictable token streaming + stable tail latency under load.
2) Reliability / graceful degradation
   - We walked through a route with fallback behavior so your app stays online if a model/region is constrained.
3) Cost controls + observability
   - Token-level cost/latency breakdowns in Console and how batching/caching settings translate into unit economics.

Links (same ones we referenced live):
- Sales Demo Quickstart (curl + SDK examples that mirror the talk track): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts
- Hosted API quickstart docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart
- Demo-tenant Security FAQ (how the demo tenant is isolated + what’s logged/retained): attached (Redwood_Demo_Tenant_Security_FAQ.pdf)

Proposed next steps for an evaluation (lightweight, 1–2 weeks):
- 30-min eval kickoff: confirm target SLOs (p50/p95), context window needs, and success metrics.
- Run a small benchmark on your top 2–3 prompts (we can start with anonymized/synthetic inputs if preferred).
- Stand up either:
  a) Hosted eval project (fastest) OR
  b) Dedicated capacity preview (if you already know you’ll need pinned throughput/isolation).

If helpful, here are two scheduling options for the kickoff:
- Fri 10:30–11:00am PT
- Mon 1:00–1:30pm PT
Or feel free to grab any slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood-se/30min-eval-kickoff

Also: you asked about “what happens to prompts during the demo.” The short version is: the demo tenant uses sanitized configurations, no customer data is expected/needed, and logging is restricted to operational telemetry needed to run the service (details in the attached FAQ). If your team wants, we can do a quick security-only follow-up with our SE + security partner present.

I’m attaching a one-pager recap as well.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_Standard_Demo_Recap_Next_Steps.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: Redwood_Demo_Tenant_Security_FAQ.pdf (PDF)


From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@northstar-ai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Ortiz <dylan.ortiz@northstar-ai.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 7:03 PM
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood Standard Demo — recap + eval next steps

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful.

A couple follow-ups from Dylan + me:
1) For the fallback routing: can we constrain it to “same model family only” (we want to avoid surprise behavior), and can we force EU-only routing later if needed?
2) What’s the best way to structure the eval so we can compare your batching/caching recommendations vs our current baseline?
3) On the security side, our team will ask about retention + access controls. The FAQ helps, but we’ll likely need a quick call.

Timing-wise, Fri 10:30am PT works for us.

Alyssa


From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@northstar-ai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Ortiz <dylan.ortiz@northstar-ai.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 9:41 AM
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood Standard Demo — recap + eval next steps

Perfect — I’ll send the invite for Fri 10:30am PT.

Quick answers ahead of the call:

1) Fallback constraints (avoid “surprise behavior”)
Yes. We can scope fallback to compatible variants only (e.g., same family / instruction-tuned equivalent), and we can set a policy so the route fails closed rather than falling back if you prefer. We’ll come prepared with two policy templates:
- “Conservative fallback” (same family only, narrow set)
- “Availability-first” (broader set, but explicitly whitelisted)
On EU-only routing: that’s supported for evals when we’re using an EU region / deployment mode; we’ll align on your data residency requirements in kickoff.

2) Eval structure (apples-to-apples baseline)
Markus will share a simple approach:
- Pick 10–20 representative prompts (or synthetic stand-ins)
- Run them in two configs: (A) baseline (no batching/caching) vs (B) recommended settings
- Compare p50/p95 latency + $/1k tokens + error rate.
We can do this in a way that’s reproducible (same prompt set, pinned model version, and the same max_tokens/temperature settings).

3) Security follow-up
Let’s add 15 minutes to the end of Fri’s call for security questions. If your team wants a separate deeper session, we can schedule that too; the usual attendees are Markus (SE) plus our security/compliance point person depending on the exact questions.

See you Friday.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
